books.section: Topic 5.9 Government Policies During the Civil War
Unit 5: Toward the Civil War and Reconstruction (1844–1877)

stimulus.source_note: Figures from Barron’s Premium AP U.S. History 2027, Chapter 7 (about $2.6 billion borrowed, about $400 million from individual savers; Legal Tender Acts 1862–1863; National Bank Acts 1863–1864; first income tax 1861) and the Gilder Lehrman Institute (about $450 million in greenbacks issued). Figures are rounded.
stimulus.text:
How the Union paid for the war (approximate figures).

| Measure | What happened |
| Borrowing | About $2.6 billion in bonds sold; about $400 million of the bonds were bought by individual savers |
| Greenbacks | About $450 million in paper money issued under the Legal Tender Acts of 1862–1863 |
| Taxes | First federal income tax levied in 1861; rates stayed modest |
| National banking | National Bank Acts of 1863–1864 created a national banking system |

source: original; stimulus as noted in stimulus.source_note
stem: The National Bank Acts of 1863 and 1864 created a national banking system. Their main purpose was to

options.text: close every bank in the South at once.
options.misconception: Background: the acts created a national banking system; they did not close Southern banks.

options.text: end all borrowing by the federal government during the war.
options.misconception: Background: the government borrowed about 2.6 billion dollars during the war; the acts did not end borrowing.

options.text: standardize bank notes and give the country a uniform currency.
replace taxes entirely with printing paper money.
options.misconception: Background: the acts reformed banking and currency; taxes and borrowing still paid for most of the war.

rationales.A: Background: the acts created a national banking system; they did not close Southern banks.
rationales.B: Background: the government borrowed about 2.6 billion dollars during the war; the acts did not end borrowing.
rationales.D: Background: the acts reformed banking and currency; taxes and borrowing still paid for most of the war.
rationales.C: The National Bank Acts created a national banking system to standardize bank notes, stabilize banking, and provide a uniform currency.
rationales.general:
1. Before the war there was no central bank, and state banks issued their own notes.
2. A war needs money that works the same in every state.
3. Background: the acts let banks join a national system and issue Treasury notes as currency.
4. One system, one kind of note, and steadier banks behind it.
Remember: a war can force a country to build the money system it lacked before.
